title: Cap. X Arg. II: Arminius's Exam of Perkins — some get only sufficient grace with foresight it will be rejected; elect get efficacious grace with foresight they will believe; God decreed not to give efficacious grace to some by reprobation
pass_a_gloss: But now in the Examination of the Perkinsian Predestination, pag. 57. etc. from the mind of Augustine, perhaps also from the sense of Scripture (for so he himself speaks) he acknowledges that unto certain men from the decree of providence there is administered grace only sufficient, and with the certain forescience of God that it is to be rejected by the free choice of man; but from the decree of predestination there is administered unto others not only sufficient grace, but efficacious, with the certain forescience of God that by the benefit of this grace those unto whom it is accommodated and applied will in very deed will, believe, and be converted. A little after: God established not to give this efficacious grace unto certain ones, and that by the decree of reprobation.
pass_b_english: But now in his Examination of Perkins's Predestination (pag. 57 etc.), from Augustine's mind — and perhaps Scripture's sense, as he himself says — he acknowledges this: to some men, from the providence decree, only sufficient grace is administered, with God's certain forescience that free choice will reject it; to others, from the predestination decree, not only sufficient grace but efficacious, with God's certain forescience that by that grace's benefit those to whom it is fitted and applied will in fact will, believe, and be converted. A little later: God established not to give this efficacious grace to certain ones — and that by the reprobation decree.
source_text: Jam vero in Examine Praedestinationis Perkinsianae, pag. 57. etc. ex mente Augustini, forte et Scripturae sensu (sic enim ipse loquitur) agnoscit quibusdam hominibus ex decreto providentiae administrari gratiam tantummodo sufficientem, ac cum certa Dei praescientia quod sit rejicienda a libero hominis arbitrio; ex decreto autem praedestinationis administrari aliis non modo sufficientem gratiam, sed efficacem, cum certa Dei praescientia fore ut beneficio hujus gratiae reipsa velint, credant et convertantur illi quibus accommodatur et adhibetur. Paulo post: Deus hanc gratiam efficacem quibusdam non dare statuit, idque decreto reprobationis.
